sources.label: Hydro
sources.blurb: Flowing or falling water drives turbines. The original renewable. Highly site-specific — every dimension has enormous variance depending on reservoir type, geography, and climate.

citation.author: U.S. Energy Information Administration
citation.title: Electric Power Monthly Table 6.07.B, Conventional Hydroelectric Annual Average

capacityFactor.note: Varies widely year-to-year depending on precipitation and snowpack. 2017 (43%) was a wet year; 2021-2024 reflect western drought. International CFs differ: Norway ~49%, Brazil ~55%.

citation.publisher: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe

landUse.note: Global median for reservoir hydro. Extreme range: 0.5 km²/TWh (run-of-river) to 300+ km²/TWh (large reservoirs in flat terrain). This is the most variable dimension across all energy sources.

citation.author: IPCC
citation.title: Climate Change 2014: Mitigation of Climate Change, Annex III Table A.III.2 — Hydropower median

lifecycleCO2.note: Includes reservoir methane emissions from decomposing vegetation. Tropical reservoirs can be 10x higher than this median.

citation.title: What are the safest and cleanest sources of energy?

citation.author: Physics Reference
citation.title: Hydropower converts gravitational potential energy — no stored chemical fuel

energyDensity.note: Hydro converts gravitational potential energy of water at height to electricity. Not a stored chemical/nuclear fuel.

constructionTime.note: Large reservoir projects average 8-12 years. Run-of-river can be 3-5 years. 8 years is a representative median.

dispatchability.label: Variable
dispatchability.note: Reservoir hydro is highly dispatchable (faster ramp than gas CC). Run-of-river is nearly intermittent. Mixed fleet → 'Variable' as a compromise category.
